key_insight: PI-GMDH adaptively builds the functional form of physics-informed representations during training, rather than fixing the architecture upfront, and applies it to incompressible Navier-Stokes flow.
engineering_relevance: This can reduce model size and training cost while preserving high accuracy for fluid-flow surrogates and inverse/forward physics-informed simulation workflows.
method: Generate candidate functional directions progressively using the first variation of the combined physics and data objective.
Optimize coefficients with block-coordinate damped Gauss-Newton updates.
Use tensor-product Chebyshev basis functions for the 2D time-dependent Taylor-Green Navier-Stokes benchmark.
evidence_signal: On the Taylor-Green benchmark, adaptive PI-GMDH achieved validation and held-out test losses of 5.299e-19 and 5.296e-19, with 204/201/175 active functions for u/v/p.
watch_item: Results come from a controlled synthetic benchmark, so the apparent gains may not directly transfer to more complex or noisy real-world CFD problems.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Method of Group Data Handling: Adaptive Construction of Functional Representations with an Application to the Navier-Stokes Equations
